PUBLISH_FLOOR_CONSEQUENCE_READ_THIS_FIRS: **maxImperviousCoverPct is a publish-floor rail (PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS, via SLATE_1B) whose hard-scoped writer (src/jobs/parcel-max-impervious-cover.mjs) refuses COUNTY_NOT_IN_SCOPE for every county but Travis and writes NO cell state there. Its cells in Bastrop, Caldwell, Hays, McLennan and Williamson are therefore `unaccounted`, which under P-252 is a REFUSAL. After the scheduler runs once under this code, requirePreBakeReadiness will refuse a publish for all five non-Travis counties of the six on that one floor rail alone -- old and new are not the same publish, and the fix is fail-closed on purpose.** The remedy is the out-of-scope not-applicable sweep reaching those counties (writeAgValuationNotApplicable is the existing precedent), which is a DATA action, forbidden to this lane (P-266/P-267). NOT MEASURED -- see dryRun. This is derived from two code reads (the writer's scope refusal, and the gate branch this PR adds), not from a store.

probeCloseGateObserved: RUN, and it GATED THIS CLOSE. First attempt, from inside this worktree: I called `scripts/enforcement/probe-close-gate.mjs`'s own evaluate() over these three files with a real reader -> { block: false, debt: [] }, i.e. 'not gated'. That reading was WRONG, and the commit proved it: the pre-commit that actually runs is not the worktree's copy. `git config core.hooksPath` in this worktree is `P:/doc_repo/.githooks` -- the CANONICAL repo outside the worktree -- and the canonical `scripts/enforcement/probe-close-gate.mjs` carries `OPS24_RANGES = [[186,198],[200,250],[252,291]]` while this worktree's copy stops at [200,250] (branch seat/dispatch-planner at c7dbc12d, canonical main at 0d9edafa). With [252,291] present, P-252 is gated AND is inside PREDICATE_DEBT, so the notApplicable branch fired and the gate printed its own debt note into the commit output verbatim: `PREDICATE DEBT (OPS-24 Law 1): _inbox/2026-09-16_p252-zero-earned-refusal_close.json: rows P-252 closed on probe.notApplicable ("build lane, PR not deployed; the integration seat grades on staging"): OPS-24 Law 1 debt, no surface predicate exists yet for these rows`. So the dispatch's sentence holds -- the hook does gate this row -- and this close is allowed on the exception the dispatch's Close section prescribed, with the debt VISIBLE rather than silent. The same commit was then REFUSED, correctly, by the FAN-DEPTH gate (A-181) for a missing top-level `subAgents {spawned, maxDepth}`; that is fixed above and the commit re-run. LESSON RECORDED, because it is the reusable part: an in-lane self-check of a control can grade a STALE copy of the control, while the copy that executes lives in the canonical repo. My first number was the wrong number and I would have filed it as fact if the commit had not contradicted it.

missionPremise: OPS-24 Law 2 (A-183): three things are called 'the gate' and the ZERO-EARNED case was still open after P-195 closed the ZERO-ROW case. Measured by violation 2026-09-16 at factory 9171279 (P-201 merged as PR #156): a county whose 65 rails ALL hold `unaccounted` cells got excluded-not-applicable on every rail (P-201 basis LIVE_ELSEWHERE), and the pre-bake rail check -- evaluatePreBakeReadiness, the rail half of the real publish refusal requirePreBakeReadiness, called by src/jobs/bastrop-publish.mjs -- clears everything that is not `verdict === "refuse"`. Only the population check stood between such a county and a publish, and that stops passing once a bake population exists. The row's own words: 'an unaccounted cell means no one has decided anything about that parcel, which is a GAP, not a scoping decision, and the gate must fail closed on it.'

LESSON: A gate's exclusion set is part of its contract (DEV_PROCESS). The pre-fix rail check cleared everything that was not the string 'refuse', which made 65 excluded verdicts functionally identical to 65 passes. Converting it to an ALLOWLIST over the two verdicts that actually mean something is the fix that generalizes: any future verdict string added to the enum refuses until someone proves it may clear a publish.

An unaccounted cell and a not-applicable cell are different sentences. not-applicable is 'no one needed to decide'; unaccounted is 'no one decided'. A gate that cannot tell them apart will always eventually publish the second as the first, because the two look identical in a boolean.

When a fix lands in a vendored copy of another repo's module, the DIVERGENCE is the artifact that needs a test, not the fix. Pin the pre-fix source next to the fixed one and assert the disagreement set is exactly the intended size, in both directions -- that is what stops a re-vendor from reverting the work silently.

A dead exported gate is a false instrument: it reads like a control and cites like one. Registering every gate-shaped export with its caller status (and asserting the registry against the source, comments stripped) turns 'we know it is not used' into something a stranger can check.

If a test asserts the defect you were dispatched to fix, the fix and the test cannot both be right -- say so in the checkpoint BEFORE writing the code, name the contradiction in the close, and let the amended test carry its own reason.
